At Amherst, you’ll thrive individually, and you’ll make the herd stronger. So what exactly are Mammoths made of?\n\nYou’re curious about people, places, and everything else.\n\nOur students lead with an inquisitive nature, exploring and embracing the unknown.\n\nYou pull things apart to find your own answers.\n\nAmherst students start by knowing something. This means that our admission decision is based solely on your achievements, talents and promise. Your and your family's financial situation does not negatively impact your consideration for admission.\n\nI’m a non-U.S. citizen. Can I be considered for admission to Amherst and financial aid?\n\nYes! Amherst College welcomes first-year and transfer applications from international students, including those under DACA, undocumented individuals, those with fragile citizenship, and non-citizen permanent residents. About 10 percent of students enrolled at Amherst are international students. We provide support services through our International Students Office. Amherst is one of the very few U.S. colleges to offer need-blind financial aid for international students, just as we do for domestic students. “Need-blind” means that, when evaluating your application, Amherst will not take into account whether you have applied for financial aid.\n\nIs financial aid available for transfer students?\n\nYes. We treat transfer applicants just like first-year applicants. You are considered for admission on a need-blind basis and your calculated need is met in full.\n\nFinancial Aid FAQs\n\nLooking for information about financial aid? Keep exploring - it's all here.
